tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a given bash command and returns its output.

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked. To poll until a condition is met, use Monitor with an until-loop (e.g. `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`) — you get a notification when the loop exits. Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around the block.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"

schema.description:
Executes a given bash command and returns its output.

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)

Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.

  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## Usage notes

- Always include a short description summarizing what the agent will do
- When the agent is done, its final report is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Trust but verify: an agent's summary describes what it intended to do, not necessarily what it did. When an agent writes or edits code, check the actual changes before reporting the work as done.
- To continue a previously spawned agent, use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name as the `to` field — that resumes it with full context. A new Agent call starts a fresh agent with no memory of prior runs (except subagent_type: "fork"), so the prompt must be self-contained.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tool access are set in its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter, or the SDK `agents` option); the `model` parameter here overrides the definition for this one call.
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since a fresh agent is not aware of the user's intent
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Agent tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a build-validator agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls.
- With `isolation: "worktree"`, the worktree is automatically cleaned up if the agent makes no changes; otherwise the path and branch are returned in the result.

## When to fork

Fork yourself (pass `subagent_type: "fork"`) when the intermediate tool output isn't worth keeping in your context. The criterion is qualitative — "will I need this output again" — not task size. Fork open-ended questions. If research can be broken into independent questions, launch parallel forks in one message. A fork beats a fresh subagent for this — it inherits context and shares your cache.

Forks are cheap because they share your prompt cache.

**Don't peek.** The tool result includes an `output_file` path — do not Read or tail it. You get a completion notification; trust it. Reading the transcript mid-flight pulls the fork's tool noise into your context, which defeats the point of forking.

**Don't race.** After launching, you know nothing about what the fork found. Never fabricate or predict fork results in any format — not as prose, summary, or structured output. The notification arrives as a user-role message in a later turn; it is never something you write yourself. If the user asks a follow-up before the notification lands, tell them the fork is still running — give status, not a guess.

**Writing a fork prompt.** Since the fork inherits your context, the prompt is a *directive* — what to do, not what the situation is. Be specific about scope: what's in, what's out, what another agent is handling. Don't re-explain background.


## Writing the prompt

Any agent other than a fork starts with zero context. Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room — it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question — prescribed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.

For fresh agents, terse command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work.

**Never delegate understanding.** Don't write "based on your findings, fix the bug" or "based on the research, implement it." Those phrases push synthesis onto the agent instead of doing it yourself. Write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

Example usage:

<example>
user: "What's left on this branch before we can ship?"
assistant: <thinking>Forking this — it's a survey question. I want the punch list, not the git output in my context.</thinking>
Agent({
  subagent_type: "fork",
  name: "ship-audit",
  description: "Branch ship-readiness audit",
  prompt: "Audit what's left before this branch can ship. Check: uncommitted changes, commits ahead of main, whether tests exist, whether the GrowthBook gate is wired up, whether CI-relevant files changed. Report a punch list — done vs. missing. Under 200 words."
})
assistant: Ship-readiness audit running.
<commentary>
Turn ends here. The coordinator knows nothing about the findings yet. What follows is a SEPARATE turn — the notification arrives from outside, as a user-role message. It is not something the coordinator writes.
</commentary>
[later turn — notification arrives as user message]
assistant: Audit's back. Three blockers: no tests for the new prompt path, GrowthBook gate wired but not in build_flags.yaml, and one uncommitted file.
</example>

<example>
user: "so is the gate wired up or not"
<commentary>
User asks mid-wait. The audit fork was launched to answer exactly this, and it hasn't returned. The coordinator does not have this answer. Give status, not a fabricated result.
</commentary>
assistant: Still waiting on the audit — that's one of the things it's checking. Should land shortly.
</example>

<example>
user: "Can you get a second opinion on whether this migration is safe?"
assistant: <thinking>I'll ask the code-reviewer agent — it won't see my analysis, so it can give an independent read.</thinking>
<commentary>
A non-fork subagent_type is specified, so the agent starts fresh. It needs full context in the prompt. The briefing explains what to assess and why.
</commentary>
Agent({
  name: "migration-review",
  description: "Independent migration review",
  subagent_type: "code-reviewer",
  prompt: "Review migration 0042_user_schema.sql for safety. Context: we're adding a NOT NULL column to a 50M-row table. Existing rows get a backfill default. I want a second opinion on whether the backfill approach is safe under concurrent writes — I've checked locking behavior but want independent verification. Report: is this safe, and if not, what specifically breaks?"
})
</example>

## plugin:figma:figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

289	      .then(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(messages.addedToBag), status: 'success' }))
290	      .catch(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE), status: 'error' }));
291	  };
292	
293	  // Normalized to a real array so every `recs.length`/`recs.map` reference below is safe without
294	  // repeating the optional chain at each call site -- `useEinstein()`'s own `recommendations`
295	  // state starts as a plain `[]` (use-einstein.js:463), which has no `.recs` property at all, so
296	  // `recommendations?.recs` reads `undefined` until the request above resolves.
297	  const recs: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct[] = recommendations?.recs ?? [];
298	
299	  const cards: ZimmProductCardProps[] = recs
300	    .map((product): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
301	      const card = selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard(product, formatPrice, buildUrl);
302	      if (!card) return null;
303	
304	      const selectedSizeChipValue = selectedSizeChipValues[product.id];
305	      return {
306	        ...card,
307	        selectedSizeChipValue,
308	        onSizeChipSelect: (value: string) =>
309	          setSelectedSizeChipValues((previous) => ({ ...previous, [product.id]: value })),
310	        onAddToBag: () => {
311	          // No selection -> default-variant behaviour (matches product-list/index.tsx's own
312	          // ProductListCard.handleAddToBag exactly): no size selected means default size. A
313	          // selection that somehow matches no real variant falls back the same way, rather than
314	          // blocking the add entirely on a data mismatch.
315	          const resolved = selectedSizeChipValue ? resolveOrderableVariant(product, selectedSizeChipValue) : null;
316	          handleResolvedAddToBag(resolved?.productId ?? product.id, resolved?.price ?? product.price);
317	        },
318	      };
319	    })
320	    .filter((card): card is RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard => card !== null);
321	
322	  const title = intl.formatMessage(messages.title);
323	
324	  return (
325	    <Box data-testid="recently-viewed-page">
326	      <Seo title={title} description={PAGE_DESCRIPTION}>
327	        <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow" />
328	      </Seo>
329	      {/* Screen-reader-only page heading — 2026-09-10, closing a real gap: this page had no
330	       * Heading element at all in either branch below, breaking the pattern product-list/index.tsx
331	       * and product-detail/index.tsx both already follow, and leaving however many real <h3>
332	       * product-name headings ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid renders (uncapped as of build plan step E4 --
333	       * see that component's own `cards` JSDoc) with nothing above them in the heading hierarchy
334	       * (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.3.1/2.4.6). `srOnly`,
335	       * matching product-detail/index.tsx's own <h1> exactly — the page's own visible title
336	       * styling (ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid's own textStyle="heading3" span, unchanged here) is a
337	       * separate, wider pre-existing pattern (several other organisms do the same thing) and out
338	       * of scope for this fix. */}
339	      <Heading as="h1" srOnly>
340	        {title}
341	      </Heading>
342	      {cards.length > 0 ? (
343	        // Bleeds the grid edge-to-edge past #app-main's own sitewide padding, matching the
344	        // Recently Viewed Rail's own flush treatment (product-detail/product-list's
345	        // <RecommendedProducts mx={PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX}>) — confirmed against this page's own
346	        // three real Figma frames (9551:78221 Desktop / 9560:137688 Tablet / 9560:138459 Mobile,
347	        // Zimmermann_Designs file), which show the header and every Product Card Group spanning
348	        // the full frame width, not inset within a page margin. ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid itself has
349	        // no passthrough/mx slot (unlike RecommendedProducts, which forwards `{...props}` to its
350	        // own wrapping Box for exactly this reason), so the bleed is applied here at the page
351	        // level instead. EmptyRecentlyViewed below is a distinct, centred layout with no
352	        // edge-to-edge requirement of its own — deliberately not wrapped the same way.
353	        //
354	        // APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX, not PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX — corrected 2026-09-10 (real, live-confirmed
355	        // bug: this page rendered wider than the viewport at every breakpoint, e.g. 1504px at a
356	        // 1440px Desktop viewport). This page has no PageContainer/layerStyle="page" second
357	        // containment layer the way PDP/PLP do — #app-main's own padding is the only thing here to
358	        // cancel — so it needs the single-layer constant, not the two-layer one. See that
359	        // constant's own comment in app/constants/index.ts for the full root-cause math.
360	        <Box
361	          mx={APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX}
362	          // Space before the global Footer — Figma's own page frames (see the mx comment above
363	          // for the node ids) show this filled by "Footer Primary" (node 9560:110769 on Desktop,
364	          // same shape on Tablet/Mobile — a "Load More" button, deferred: real, Figma-annotated
365	          // functional requirement, not built yet, Marcel 2026-09-10), uniformly 32px top-padding +
366	          // 52px button + 80px bottom-padding = 164px on all three breakpoints, sitting flush
367	          // against both the last card row above it and the real Footer below it (zero extra gap
368	          // either side, confirmed directly). With no button to render, only the padding portion
369	          // is reserved here (32+80=112px, Marcel's own call, 2026-09-10) — not the button's own
370	          // 52px, since there's nothing occupying that height right now. This will need to grow by
371	          // that 52px once Load More is actually built; that future component replaces this
372	          // padding entirely rather than sitting alongside it.
373	          paddingBottom="calc(var(--zimm-scale-800) + var(--zimm-scale-5xl))" // 32px + 80px = 112px
374	        >
375	          <ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid
376	            title={title}
377	            itemCountLabel={intl.formatMessage(messages.itemCount, { count: cards.length })}
378	            cards={cards}
379	          />
380	        </Box>
381	      ) : !isLoading && cards.length === 0 ? (
382	        <EmptyRecentlyViewed isRegistered={isRegistered} />
383	      ) : null}
384	    </Box>
385	  );
386	};
387	
388	RecentlyViewed.getTemplateName = () => 'recently-viewed';
389	
390	export default RecentlyViewed;

17	 * separate flat Einstein image to fall back to, so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no
18	 * usable `src`" and "there is no usable image at all" were the same case.
19	 *
20	 * **Superseded 2026-09-15 (build plan step E1, formalised by step E4): input is once again the
21	 * Einstein rec, not a plain Commerce API product.** The interim fetch utility and its companion
22	 * history-tracking hook referenced above are deleted as of build plan step E4 (see
23	 * `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own module docblock for the full "why"). Einstein's own
24	 * `fetchRecProductDetails` (`use-einstein.js:465-520`) already merges each rec with its full
25	 * hydrated `getProducts` record before this mapper ever sees it (`{...rec, ...product, productId,
26	 * image}`) — a strict superset of the plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` shape this mapper read
27	 * during the interim period described above, so nothing below needed a functional change; this
28	 * note is the only edit build plan step E4 made to this file.
29	 *
30	 * Modelled on `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` — no React/react-intl import,
31	 * `formatPrice` injected as a parameter so this module stays independently testable — and on the
32	 * general shape of `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (`feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`, not this
33	 * branch — read for its approach, not imported). Unlike that demo mapper, this is a production
34	 * path: real `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` SDK types are used directly (AGENTS.md > Type
35	 * Definitions) — with the Einstein-specific input shape gone, there is no longer any hand-rolled
36	 * field on the input type at all.
37	 *
38	 * Deliberately narrow scope, stated here rather than left as a silent gap: this mapper only ever
39	 * returns `currentPrice` (an active selling price), not was/now sale-price detection
40	 * (`originalPrice`) — but that is a scope choice, not a data limitation. **Correction
41	 * (2026-09-08, pre-dates and is unaffected by the input-source revision above):** an earlier
42	 * version of this comment claimed the merged Einstein shape "has no equivalent of"
43	 * `getPriceData`-style pricebook logic — verified inaccurate, and equally true of the plain
44	 * `getProducts` shape this mapper read during the interim period: that now-removed fetch utility
45	 * already requested `perPricebook: true`, so `product.tieredPrices` was present, and base SFCC's `getPriceData`
46	 * (`app/utils/product-utils.js`) already derives `listPrice`/`isOnSale` from exactly that field —

48	 * that the `recentlyViewed` variation renders no price at all today (see
49	 * `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s `recentlyViewed` `VARIATION_CONFIG` row — `showContent: false`), so
50	 * there is nothing for it to feed. Mapping `currentPrice` anyway costs nothing and means a future
51	 * consumer of this same mapper (e.g. a variation that does render price) isn't blocked on this
52	 * file being revisited — extending it to also call `getPriceData` at that point would be a small,
53	 * well-precedented addition, not new pricebook work.

55	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
56	import { filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
57	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
58	import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardImage } from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
59	import { sortImagesBySequence, resolveFallbackColour, resolveRequiredAlt } from './productCardMappingHelpers';
60	
61	/**
62	 * The real Commerce API `Product` (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
63	 * — not hand-rolled). A plain alias, not an augmentation: the Einstein rec this mapper reads again
64	 * as of build plan step E1/E4 needs nothing bolted on either — `Product.id` is used directly, and
65	 * there is no separate flat-image field to reconcile. Kept as a
66	 * named alias (rather than importing `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` directly at each call site)
67	 * so this module's own input type has a name that documents its role here.
68	 */
69	export type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product;
70	
71	/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl,
72	 *  mirroring `productInfo.ts`'s own `FormatPrice` shape. */
73	export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
74	
75	/**
76	 * The subset of `ZimmProductCardBaseProps` this mapper populates. Deliberately excludes
77	 * `headingLevel` and `variation` — both are render-context decisions belonging to the container
78	 * step that maps recs through this mapper and renders the rail (SFCC-83's A6 step), which supplies
79	 * `headingLevel` uniformly for every card and adds `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` itself when
80	 * spreading this output into `<ZimmProductCard>` — the rail organism itself (A5) takes already-full
81	 * `ZimmProductCardProps` objects, so variation must already be set before it sees them. A pure data
82	 * mapper choosing a heading level would conflate a data concern with a layout one. Also excludes `hoverImage`/`images` — this
83	 * mapper only ever returns one image (`primaryImage`); see `selectPrimaryImage`'s own docblock
84	 * for why.
85	 */
86	export type RecentlyViewedCard = Pick<
87	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
88	  'id' | 'href' | 'name' | 'primaryImage' | 'currentPrice'
89	>;
90	
91	/** The correctly-sized product image view, per AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance: never serve an
92	 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size. Named rather than inlined per conventions.md's
93	 *  no-magic-strings rule — this is a real, semantic SFCC image `viewType` key. */
94	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
95	
96	/** The variation-attribute id `filterImageGroups` matches an image group's colour against — same
97	 *  constant, same reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own. */
98	const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
99	
100	/** The one shape this mapper sorts — whatever `ImageGroup.images` actually holds. */
101	type ImageGroupImage = NonNullable<ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup['images']>[number];
102	
103	/**
104	 * Sorts by the merchandiser-assigned sequence number baked into each image's own filename
105	 * (e.g. `.../images/1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` → `1`) — confirmed live on `4673TS251`,
106	 * whose colour-tagged medium group came back `[2, 1, 3, ...]`, which silently showed the on-model
107	 * shot (image `2`) as primary instead of the flat-lay shot (always image `1`).
108	 *
109	 * Shared with `productListCardMapper.ts` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — see
110	 * `productCardMappingHelpers.ts`'s own docblock for why a shared primitive rather than three
111	 * separate copies (all three had drifted onto the identical non-transitive-comparator bug,
112	 * CodeRabbit 2026-09-10). This file's own images are the raw SDK shape (`disBaseLink`/`link`,
113	 * not a flat `src`), hence the explicit accessor.
114	 */
115	const sortByImageSequence = (images: ImageGroupImage[]): ImageGroupImage[] =>
116	  sortImagesBySequence(images, (image) => image.disBaseLink || image.link || '');
117	
118	/**
119	 * Resolves which real colour this product's one image should come from — now the shared
120	 * `resolveFallbackColour` (`productCardMappingHelpers.ts`) directly, since there is no
121	 * `representedProduct` branch to add here: this input is a plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
122	 * (from `getProducts`), which has no such field at all (confirmed against the SDK's own type).
123	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveRepresentativeColour` layers exactly one extra branch
124	 * (a `representedProduct` match, Search-hit-only) in front of this same shared fallback.
125	 * Returns `undefined` when there are no variants at all — `selectPrimaryImage` below then falls
126	 * back to an unscoped, viewtype-only lookup, never a throw.
127	 */
128	const resolveViewedColour = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct): string | undefined =>
129	  resolveFallbackColour(product.variants, COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
130	
131	/**
132	 * Resolves the one image this mapper ever returns. `hoverImage`/`images` are never populated —
133	 * SFCC-83 AC 3 asks for "the product's index image" (singular), and the `recentlyViewed`
134	 * variation renders neither a hover-swap nor a gallery (see `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
135	 * `recentlyViewed` row: `showHoverImageSwap: false`, and its render branch never forwards
136	 * `images` at all).
137	 *
138	 * Uses `filterImageGroups` at `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image),
139	 * **colour-scoped first, then viewtype-only as a fallback** — same two-pass fix, same reasoning,
140	 * as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectColourScopedImages`, closing a real bug confirmed
141	 * live on `4673TS251`: with no colour scoping at all, an older, untagged, genuinely-404 medium
142	 * group and a newer, correctly colour-tagged one are both candidates, and the untagged one wins by
143	 * default purely because it happens to sit first in the API's own array order. Scoping by colour
144	 * excludes the untagged group outright. The fallback pass exists for the opposite real case — a
145	 * genuinely single-colour product whose one medium group carries no `variationAttributes` tag at
146	 * all (nothing to disambiguate) — which a strict colour-scoped lookup alone would exclude and
147	 * return nothing for. Never the reverse: a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
148	 * avoid re-mixing colours.
149	 *
150	 * **No flat-image fallback (2026-09-08 input-source revision).** The pre-revision Einstein-merged
151	 * shape carried its own flat `image.disBaseLink`/`image.alt` (Einstein's own single-reference
152	 * thumbnail) to fall back to when `imageGroups` filtering came up empty. The plain
153	 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads has no equivalent field at all — `imageGroups` is the
154	 * only image source there is — so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no usable `src`" and
155	 * "there is no usable image at all" have collapsed into the same case; both now return `null`.
156	 *
157	 * @returns `null` when there is no usable `src`. `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and
158	 *   non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image — "no usable
159	 *   image" is treated the same as "no usable name" in `selectRecentlyViewedCard` below: a hard
160	 *   gate that yields no card at all. Returning `null` here is the only option that structurally
161	 *   cannot violate the non-empty-`alt` contract, since there is no returned object for `alt` to
162	 *   be empty on.
163	 */
164	const selectPrimaryImage = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct, productName: string): ZimmProductCardImage | null => {
165	  const colour = resolveViewedColour(product);
166	
167	  const colourScopedGroups = colour
168	    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
169	        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
170	        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
171	      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
172	    : [];
173	
174	  const groups =
175	    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
176	      ? colourScopedGroups
177	      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
178	          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
179	        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);
180	
181	  const [groupImage] = sortByImageSequence(groups[0]?.images ?? []);
182	  if (!groupImage) return null;
183	
184	  const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
185	  if (!src) return null;
186	
187	  // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required and non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's
188	  // decorative alt: '' convention) — shared resolveRequiredAlt (productCardMappingHelpers.ts).
189	  const alt = resolveRequiredAlt(groupImage.alt, productName);
190	  return { src, alt };
191	};
192	
193	/**
194	 * @param product - A Commerce-API-product-shaped value — as of build plan step E1/E4, the Einstein
195	 *   recommendation object `fetchRecProductDetails` returns (a strict superset of the plain
196	 *   `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` this mapper is typed against) — or `undefined`/`null` while
197	 *   that data is not yet available.
198	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
199	 * @param buildUrl - Site/locale prefixer, normally `useMultiSite()`'s own `buildUrl`. Fixed
200	 *   2026-09-15 (CodeRabbit finding, confirmed): `productUrlBuilder` alone only ever returns a bare
201	 *   `/product/:id` path with no site/locale awareness, and `ZimmProductCard`'s `recentlyViewed`
202	 *   render branch links via a plain `react-router-dom` `Link` (`zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
203	 *   `MediaOnlyCardLink`), not the base SFCC `Link` that would otherwise apply this prefix
204	 *   internally — so a shopper on a non-default site/locale previously always landed on the
205	 *   default site/locale instead of the storefront they were actually browsing. Same fix, same
206	 *   reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectProductListCard`
207	 *   (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts:273,290`) — injected as a
208	 *   parameter for the same reason `formatPrice` already is: this stays a pure function with no
209	 *   hook dependency of its own.
210	 * @returns Props for the `recentlyViewed` `ZimmProductCard` variation, or `null` when the product
211	 *   has no usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw.
212	 */
213	export const selectRecentlyViewedCard = (
214	  product: RecentlyViewedProduct | undefined | null,
215	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
216	  buildUrl: (path: string) => string,
217	): RecentlyViewedCard | null => {
218	  if (!product?.name) return null;
219	
220	  const primaryImage = selectPrimaryImage(product, product.name);
221	  if (!primaryImage) return null;
222	
223	  return {
224	    id: product.id,
225	    href: buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id })),
226	    name: product.name,
227	    primaryImage,
228	    // No hardcoded fallback currency — if either is absent, skip formatting rather than guess,
229	    // matching productInfo.ts's own "no hardcoded fallback currency" comment.
230	    currentPrice:
231	      typeof product.price === 'number' && product.currency ? formatPrice(product.price, product.currency) : undefined,
232	  };
233	};

import { filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardImage } from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
import { sortImagesBySequence, resolveFallbackColour, resolveRequiredAlt } from './productCardMappingHelpers';

/**
 * The real Commerce API `Product` (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
 * — not hand-rolled). A plain alias, not an augmentation: the Einstein rec this mapper reads again
 * as of build plan step E1/E4 needs nothing bolted on either — `Product.id` is used directly, and
 * there is no separate flat-image field to reconcile. Kept as a
 * named alias (rather than importing `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` directly at each call site)
 * so this module's own input type has a name that documents its role here.
 */
export type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product;

/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl,
 *  mirroring `productInfo.ts`'s own `FormatPrice` shape. */
export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;

/**
 * The subset of `ZimmProductCardBaseProps` this mapper populates. Deliberately excludes
 * `headingLevel` and `variation` — both are render-context decisions belonging to the container
 * step that maps recs through this mapper and renders the rail (SFCC-83's A6 step), which supplies
 * `headingLevel` uniformly for every card and adds `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` itself when
 * spreading this output into `<ZimmProductCard>` — the rail organism itself (A5) takes already-full
 * `ZimmProductCardProps` objects, so variation must already be set before it sees them. A pure data
 * mapper choosing a heading level would conflate a data concern with a layout one. Also excludes `hoverImage`/`images` — this
 * mapper only ever returns one image (`primaryImage`); see `selectPrimaryImage`'s own docblock
 * for why.
 */
export type RecentlyViewedCard = Pick<
  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
  'id' | 'href' | 'name' | 'primaryImage' | 'currentPrice'
>;

/** The correctly-sized product image view, per AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance: never serve an
 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size. Named rather than inlined per conventions.md's
 *  no-magic-strings rule — this is a real, semantic SFCC image `viewType` key. */
const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';

/** The variation-attribute id `filterImageGroups` matches an image group's colour against — same
 *  constant, same reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own. */
const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';

/** The one shape this mapper sorts — whatever `ImageGroup.images` actually holds. */
type ImageGroupImage = NonNullable<ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup['images']>[number];

/**
 * Sorts by the merchandiser-assigned sequence number baked into each image's own filename
 * (e.g. `.../images/1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` → `1`) — confirmed live on `4673TS251`,
 * whose colour-tagged medium group came back `[2, 1, 3, ...]`, which silently showed the on-model
 * shot (image `2`) as primary instead of the flat-lay shot (always image `1`).
 *
 * Shared with `productListCardMapper.ts` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — see
 * `productCardMappingHelpers.ts`'s own docblock for why a shared primitive rather than three
 * separate copies (all three had drifted onto the identical non-transitive-comparator bug,
 * CodeRabbit 2026-09-10). This file's own images are the raw SDK shape (`disBaseLink`/`link`,
 * not a flat `src`), hence the explicit accessor.
 */
const sortByImageSequence = (images: ImageGroupImage[]): ImageGroupImage[] =>
  sortImagesBySequence(images, (image) => image.disBaseLink || image.link || '');

/**
 * Resolves which real colour this product's one image should come from — now the shared
 * `resolveFallbackColour` (`productCardMappingHelpers.ts`) directly, since there is no
 * `representedProduct` branch to add here: this input is a plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
 * (from `getProducts`), which has no such field at all (confirmed against the SDK's own type).
 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveRepresentativeColour` layers exactly one extra branch
 * (a `representedProduct` match, Search-hit-only) in front of this same shared fallback.
 * Returns `undefined` when there are no variants at all — `selectPrimaryImage` below then falls
 * back to an unscoped, viewtype-only lookup, never a throw.
 */
const resolveViewedColour = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct): string | undefined =>
  resolveFallbackColour(product.variants, COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);

/**
 * Resolves the one image this mapper ever returns. `hoverImage`/`images` are never populated —
 * SFCC-83 AC 3 asks for "the product's index image" (singular), and the `recentlyViewed`
 * variation renders neither a hover-swap nor a gallery (see `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
 * `recentlyViewed` row: `showHoverImageSwap: false`, and its render branch never forwards
 * `images` at all).
 *
 * Uses `filterImageGroups` at `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image),
 * **colour-scoped first, then viewtype-only as a fallback** — same two-pass fix, same reasoning,
 * as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectColourScopedImages`, closing a real bug confirmed
 * live on `4673TS251`: with no colour scoping at all, an older, untagged, genuinely-404 medium
 * group and a newer, correctly colour-tagged one are both candidates, and the untagged one wins by
 * default purely because it happens to sit first in the API's own array order. Scoping by colour
 * excludes the untagged group outright. The fallback pass exists for the opposite real case — a
 * genuinely single-colour product whose one medium group carries no `variationAttributes` tag at
 * all (nothing to disambiguate) — which a strict colour-scoped lookup alone would exclude and
 * return nothing for. Never the reverse: a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
 * avoid re-mixing colours.
 *
 * **No flat-image fallback (2026-09-08 input-source revision).** The pre-revision Einstein-merged
 * shape carried its own flat `image.disBaseLink`/`image.alt` (Einstein's own single-reference
 * thumbnail) to fall back to when `imageGroups` filtering came up empty. The plain
 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads has no equivalent field at all — `imageGroups` is the
 * only image source there is — so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no usable `src`" and
 * "there is no usable image at all" have collapsed into the same case; both now return `null`.
 *
 * @returns `null` when there is no usable `src`. `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and
 *   non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image — "no usable
 *   image" is treated the same as "no usable name" in `selectRecentlyViewedCard` below: a hard
 *   gate that yields no card at all. Returning `null` here is the only option that structurally
 *   cannot violate the non-empty-`alt` contract, since there is no returned object for `alt` to
 *   be empty on.
 */
const selectPrimaryImage = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct, productName: string): ZimmProductCardImage | null => {
  const colour = resolveViewedColour(product);

  const colourScopedGroups = colour
    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
    : [];

  const groups =
    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
      ? colourScopedGroups
      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);

  const [groupImage] = sortByImageSequence(groups[0]?.images ?? []);
  if (!groupImage) return null;

  const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
  if (!src) return null;

  // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required and non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's
  // decorative alt: '' convention) — shared resolveRequiredAlt (productCardMappingHelpers.ts).
  const alt = resolveRequiredAlt(groupImage.alt, productName);
  return { src, alt };
};

/**
 * @param product - A Commerce-API-product-shaped value — as of build plan step E1/E4, the Einstein
 *   recommendation object `fetchRecProductDetails` returns (a strict superset of the plain
 *   `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` this mapper is typed against) — or `undefined`/`null` while
 *   that data is not yet available.
 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
 * @param buildUrl - Site/locale prefixer, normally `useMultiSite()`'s own `buildUrl`. Fixed
 *   2026-09-15 (CodeRabbit finding, confirmed): `productUrlBuilder` alone only ever returns a bare
 *   `/product/:id` path with no site/locale awareness, and `ZimmProductCard`'s `recentlyViewed`
 *   render branch links via a plain `react-router-dom` `Link` (`zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
 *   `MediaOnlyCardLink`), not the base SFCC `Link` that would otherwise apply this prefix
 *   internally — so a shopper on a non-default site/locale previously always landed on the
 *   default site/locale instead of the storefront they were actually browsing. Same fix, same
 *   reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectProductListCard`
 *   (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts:273,290`) — injected as a
 *   parameter for the same reason `formatPrice` already is: this stays a pure function with no
 *   hook dependency of its own.
 * @returns Props for the `recentlyViewed` `ZimmProductCard` variation, or `null` when the product
 *   has no usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw.
 */
export const selectRecentlyViewedCard = (
  product: RecentlyViewedProduct | undefined | null,
  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
  buildUrl: (path: string) => string,
): RecentlyViewedCard | null => {
  if (!product?.name) return null;

  const primaryImage = selectPrimaryImage(product, product.name);
  if (!primaryImage) return null;

  return {
    id: product.id,
    href: buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id })),
    name: product.name,
    primaryImage,
    // No hardcoded fallback currency — if either is absent, skip formatting rather than guess,
    // matching productInfo.ts's own "no hardcoded fallback currency" comment.
    currentPrice:
      typeof product.price === 'number' && product.currency ? formatPrice(product.price, product.currency) : undefined,
  };
};

230	 * strict colour-scoped `filterImageGroups` match requires the group to explicitly declare a
231	 * matching `variationAttributes` entry, but a single-colour product's medium group commonly
232	 * carries no `variationAttributes` at all (nothing to disambiguate), which would make a
233	 * colour-scoped-only lookup exclude the group and return nothing. Falls back to a viewtype-only
234	 * match in that case. Never the reverse — a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
235	 * avoid re-mixing colours.
236	 */
237	const selectColourScopedImages = (
238	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
239	  colour: string | undefined,
240	): ZimmProductCardImage[] => {
241	  const colourScopedGroups = colour
242	    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
243	        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
244	        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
245	      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
246	    : [];
247	
248	  const groups =
249	    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
250	      ? colourScopedGroups
251	      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
252	          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
253	        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);
254	
255	  const images = (groups[0]?.images ?? [])
256	    .map(toCardImage)
257	    .filter((image): image is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(image));
258	
259	  return sortByImageSequence(images);
260	};
261	
262	/**
263	 * Picks this product's gallery from the colour-scoped image list above — matches
264	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for 0 or 1 images (returns `undefined`, never
265	 * a 1-length array). Kept exported and independently tested, same as
266	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectGalleryImages` — `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`
267	 * below calls `selectColourScopedImages` directly instead (one shared computation feeding
268	 * `primaryImage`/`primaryImageFallbacks`/`hoverImage`/`images` at once), matching that file's own
269	 * documented, deliberate minor redundancy rather than introducing a new one.
270	 */
271	export const selectGalleryImages = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
272	  const images = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
273	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
274	};
275	
276	/**
277	 * Reads the "size" variation attribute (if this product has one) into the shape
278	 * `ZimmSizeChipGroup` expects. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
279	 * `selectSizeChipValues`, re-pointed at `product.variationAttributes` directly — `orderable` on
280	 * each value already reflects real stock for that specific size, so it maps directly to
281	 * `isDisabled` with no extra lookup needed.
282	 */
283	export const selectSizeChipValues = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmSizeChipValue[] => {
284	  const sizeAttribute = product.variationAttributes?.find((attr) => attr.id === SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
285	  return (sizeAttribute?.values ?? []).map((value) => ({
286	    value: value.value,
287	    label: value.name ?? value.value,
288	    isDisabled: value.orderable === false,
289	  }));
290	};
291	
292	/** What `resolveOrderableVariant` resolves a selected size chip value to — same shape, same
293	 *  reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ResolvedVariant`: the real, orderable SKU for
294	 *  that specific size, not the master id this product otherwise defaults to. */
295	export type ResolvedVariant = {
296	  productId: string;
297	  price: number | undefined;
298	  orderable: boolean;
299	};
300	
301	/**
302	 * Resolves a selected size CHIP VALUE to its real orderable variant — ported near-verbatim from
303	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveOrderableVariant`, re-pointed at this input's own
304	 * `variants` field (identical shape either way — both are `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` `Variant`
305	 * types). Returns `null` when there is no matching variant at all — callers fall back to this
306	 * product's own default id/price in that case, the same default that already existed before
307	 * size-aware Add to Bag was ever selectable.
308	 */
309	export const resolveOrderableVariant = (
310	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
311	  sizeValue: string,
312	): ResolvedVariant | null => {
313	  const variant = product.variants?.find((candidate) => candidate.variationValues?.size === sizeValue);
314	  if (!variant) return null;
315	
316	  return {
317	    productId: variant.productId,
318	    price: variant.price,
319	    orderable: variant.orderable !== false,
320	  };
321	};
322	
323	/**
324	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(product)` call — see this
325	 * module's own docblock for why both must come from the same call rather than mixing a flat
326	 * `product.price` field for one and `getPriceData` for the other. No `opts` passed — the default
327	 * `quantity: 1` is correct for a single-unit card display (matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
328	 * no-opts calls for the same reason). No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
329	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed, matching `productInfo.ts`'s and
330	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own "no hardcoded fallback currency" rule.
331	 */
332	const selectPriceFields = (
333	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
334	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
335	): Pick<RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
336	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(product);
337	
338	  const currentPrice =
339	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && product.currency
340	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, product.currency)
341	      : undefined;
342	
343	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale product must not render a crossed-out price
344	  // identical to its current one.
345	  const originalPrice =
346	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && product.currency
347	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, product.currency)
348	      : undefined;
349	
350	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
351	};
352	
353	/**
354	 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product shape (Einstein's own merged rec, superseding
355	 *   the interim build's own dedicated fetch utility, since removed, finding #11), or
356	 *   `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
357	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
358	 * @param buildUrl - Site/locale prefixer, normally `useMultiSite()`'s own `buildUrl`. Fixed
359	 *   2026-09-15 (CodeRabbit finding, confirmed): `productUrlBuilder` alone only ever returns a bare
360	 *   `/product/:id` path with no site/locale awareness, and `ZimmProductCard`'s `plp` render branch
361	 *   (this mapper's own output variation) has no other mechanism that would rescue that — so a
362	 *   shopper on a non-default site/locale previously always landed on the default site/locale
363	 *   instead of the storefront they were actually browsing. Same fix, same reasoning, as
364	 *   `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectProductListCard`
365	 *   (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts:273,290`) and as
366	 *   `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectRecentlyViewedCard` — injected as a parameter for the
367	 *   same reason `formatPrice` already is: this stays a pure function with no hook dependency of
368	 *   its own.
369	 * @returns Props for the `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard`, or `null` when the product has no
370	 *   usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw. Same hard-gate contract
371	 *   as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectRecentlyViewedCard`. `onAddToBag`/`selectedSizeChipValue`/
372	 *   `onSizeChipSelect` are deliberately not populated here — same split
373	 *   `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult` documents: this mapper is a pure data
374	 *   function with no per-card selection state of its own, so the page container wires those three
375	 *   (see `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own per-card size-chip state).
376	 */
377	export const selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = (
378	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct | undefined | null,
379	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
380	  buildUrl: (path: string) => string,
381	): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
382	  if (!product?.name) return null;
383	
384	  // One resolution feeds primaryImage, the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the broken-image
385	  // fallback candidates below — see selectColourScopedImages's own docblock for why.
386	  const scopedImages = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
387	  const [firstImage] = scopedImages;
388	  if (!firstImage) return null;
389	
390	  // Required-non-empty alt for the primary position only — shared resolveRequiredAlt
391	  // (productCardMappingHelpers.ts, also used by recentlyViewedCard.ts's own primary image). Was
392	  // `firstImage.alt || product.name` here (no `.trim()`) until 2026-09-10, a real gap this shared
393	  // helper closes: a whitespace-only alt is a non-empty string, so it passed straight through
394	  // instead of falling back — confirmed with a real whitespace-only-alt repro. The rest of
395	  // scopedImages keeps toCardImage's plain alt (matching productListCardMapper.ts's own gallery
396	  // images, which get no such treatment either) since only the primary slot ever carried this
397	  // extra safeguard.
398	  const primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage = { ...firstImage, alt: resolveRequiredAlt(firstImage.alt, product.name) };
399	
400	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(product, formatPrice);
401	
402	  return {
403	    id: product.id,
404	    href: buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id })),
405	    name: product.name,
406	    headingLevel: 'h3',
407	    primaryImage,
408	    // Ordered backup candidates if primaryImage itself fails to load — same real, live defect
409	    // productListCardMapper.ts's own primaryImageFallbacks closes.
410	    primaryImageFallbacks: scopedImages,
411	    // The second image in the same colour-scoped sequence — revealed on hover. undefined when
412	    // there is no second image, which ZimmProductCardMedia already treats as "no swap".
413	    hoverImage: scopedImages[1],
414	    images: scopedImages.length > 1 ? scopedImages : undefined,
415	    currentPrice,
416	    originalPrice,
417	    // product.master is this master product's own overall orderability (ShopperProductsTypes.Master
418	    // — confirmed via the SDK's own type) — the equivalent of productListCardMapper.ts's flat
419	    // hit.orderable for this input shape, which has no such flat field of its own.
420	    isUnavailable: product.master?.orderable === false,
421	    // Single highest-priority badge -- confirmed live, 2026-09-09 (see this module's own docblock's
422	    // "Badge" section). SFCC-225's own hook already sorts c_productBadges by badgePriorityOrder
423	    // before this ever reaches the frontend, matching productListCardMapper.ts's own identical read.
424	    badge: product.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge,
425	    variation: 'plp',
426	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(product),
427	  };
428	};

content.text: This is a significant lead — before I fan out sub-agents, let me directly verify a specific hypothesis: the CR-fix commit `5660869` fixed a "gate on raw recs, not mapped cards" bug in the page (E2), but I need to check whether the identical bug shape still exists, unfixed, in the rail (E1).

input.command: git show 5660869 --stat && echo "---FULL DIFF---" && git show 5660869
input.description: Show the CR-fix commit that gated the page on mapped cards

content.content:
commit 56608692fbd90c86352080aa5b96197ffe890cc6
Author: Marcel Angelo Navarro <marcel.a.n.navarro@accenture.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 15 10:31:31 2026 +0800

    fix(recently-viewed): gate the Full History page on mapped cards, skip Cart's wasted Einstein call
    
    Two findings from this branch's own local CodeRabbit Final Gate pass
    (cr review --light --base develop), both confirmed against real code
    before fixing -- 7 other findings from that same pass were confirmed
    to predate this branch (diffed against c14ee9f, the fork point) and
    belong to feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed / PR #107's own scope,
    not fixed here.
    
    recentlyViewed/index.tsx: the render gate checked recs.length (raw
    Einstein count) instead of cards.length (count after
    selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard's null-filtering map). If every
    rec fails to map to a card -- e.g. every product now offline or
    deleted -- recs.length stayed truthy, so the grid branch rendered
    ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid with an empty cards array (which renders
    null by its own contract), and the empty-state branch never got a
    chance to fire either, since it checked the same recs.length. A
    shopper with real but entirely stale history saw a blank page. Both
    branch conditions now check cards.length instead. cards is a plain
    synchronous map/filter over recs in the same render with no
    separate state or effect, so this closes the gap without
    reintroducing any async race. New test proves it, mutation-tested:
    reverted the fix, confirmed the new test fails for the claimed
    reason, restored, confirmed green. A pre-existing test was already
    sitting on this exact edge case (returning null from the card mapper
    for every product) but only asserted "does an h1 render" -- true
    regardless of branch -- so it never caught the bug; corrected to
    assert the actual branch rendered.
    
    recommended-products/index.tsx: the fetch effect fired
    getRecommendations unconditionally on the Cart route for the
    Recently-Viewed recommender, even though the render branch always
    returns null there and never reads the result. Named as an accepted,
    optional cleanup in the original build plan ("may keep a Cart-only
    skip if trivial; not required") -- now skipped outright. One
    existing test asserted the old wasted-call behaviour as accepted;
    updated to assert the call no longer happens.
    
    Verified: tsc clean; test 85 files/1306 tests (up from 1305 -- the
    one new edge-case test); lint 8 errors/43 warnings (identical);
    audit:tokens 3 unacknowledged (identical). Re-ran the local
    CodeRabbit review against this diff afterward: all 4 findings it
    returned are on code neither this fix nor the branch's own E1-E4
    commits touched, confirmed against the fork point -- nothing new
    introduced.

1	import React from 'react';
2	import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
3	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
4	import { Link as RouteLink } from 'react-router-dom';
5	import { useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount } from 'app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount';
6	import { ZimmProductCard } from '../zimmProductCard';
7	import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation } from '../zimmProductCard';
8	
9	/**
10	 * The narrow `recentlyViewed`-only slice of the full `ZimmProductCardProps` union — this
11	 * component only ever renders that one variation (see this file's own module docblock), so
12	 * `cards` below is typed against exactly that, not the full four-variation union (narrowed
13	 * 2026-09-15, CodeRabbit finding, confirmed: the wider union let a caller pass e.g. a
14	 * `plp`-shaped card with no compile error, even though nothing here would ever render its
15	 * `plp`-only fields). Both halves are real, already-exported types from `zimmProductCard` —
16	 * see that module's own `ZimmProductCardBaseProps`/`ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation`.
17	 */
18	export type ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation;
19	
20	// Same `chakra(RouteLink)` wrap this component family already establishes for its own internal
21	// links (zimmProductCard/index.tsx's `MediaOnlyCardLink`, zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx's
22	// `ProductNameLink`) — used here for the See-Full-History link, which navigates to the SFCC-84
23	// Recently Viewed Full History page, an internal route, not an external URL.
24	const SeeAllLink = chakra(RouteLink);
25	
26	export type ZimmRecentlyViewedRailProps = {
27	  /**
28	   * Typed as `ReactNode`, not `string` — this component owns no copy/intl (the container, A6,
29	   * does). **Styling resolved 2026-09-08** (was previously left unstyled pending confirmation —
30	   * live Storybook testing caught the resulting bug: the title rendered in the ambient body
31	   * weight, Futura Round 400, instead of the design's intended weight): this component now
32	   * applies `textStyle="heading3"` itself when rendering `title`, matching the exact spec
33	   * confirmed against the Full History page's own title bar this same session (Figma
34	   * `Default/h3-strong` — Futura Round, 16px/18 line-height, weight 500, letter-spacing -0.12px,
35	   * uppercase — cross-checked against this codebase's registered `heading3` token, an exact
36	   * match). Applying it here rather than requiring every caller to pre-style the title guarantees
37	   * the design intent regardless of what a caller passes; a caller supplying an already fully
38	   * styled element can still override any of this via its own more-specific styling.
39	   */
40	  title: ReactNode;
41	  /**
42	   * Rendered in the exact order received (AC 2: most-recent-first, left to right) — no sorting or
43	   * reordering happens here. Capped to `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS` for the current real
44	   * breakpoint regardless of length — a hard cap, not a "fits before scrolling" soft limit (see
45	   * that constant's own comment, app/constants/index.ts, and this component's own render-body
46	   * comment below for why the cap has to live here rather than in the request that produced this
47	   * array).
48	   */
49	  cards: readonly ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps[];
50	  /** Href to the SFCC-84 Recently Viewed Full History page. The See-Full-History link only
51	   *  renders when this is provided — see the render body below. */
52	  seeAllHref?: string;
53	  /**
54	   * No default/fallback text is supplied when this is omitted while `seeAllHref` is provided —
55	   * this component owns no copy or intl (see the module docblock), so inventing an English
56	   * fallback here would risk shipping untranslated text on non-English storefronts. In real usage
57	   * the container (A6) is expected to always supply this alongside `seeAllHref`.
58	   */
59	  seeAllLabel?: string;
60	};
61	
62	const ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_RECIPE = 'ZimmRecentlyViewedRail';
63	
64	/**
65	 * SFCC-83 — the Recently Viewed rail organism (build plan section A5). Purely presentational:
66	 * data arrives as props, no data-fetching, no `useEinstein`, no `useIntl` — see
67	 * .claude/rules/components.md's container/presentational split. The container (A6) is
68	 * responsible for building `cards` (via A3's Einstein-rec-to-card mapper), gating this
69	 * component's visibility (A4's `hasRecentlyViewed`), and supplying `title`/`seeAllLabel` copy.
70	 *
71	 * Structure mirrors Figma exactly: a `header` row (title left, the See-Full-History link right)
72	 * above a `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s. No rail-level arrow buttons — `ZimmProductCardMedia`
73	 * already carries its own intra-card carousel arrows, and a second set at the rail level would
74	 * collide with them (see zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own docblock for the Figma node
75	 * evidence).
76	 *
77	 * **`group`'s horizontal scroll/scroll-snap (zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts) is a narrow-viewport
78	 * safety net, not the "more cards exist, scroll to see them" mechanism it might look like.**
79	 * Confirmed with Marcel (2026-09-08): the per-breakpoint card count below is a hard cap — a
80	 * shopper on a real, design-reference-width device never has more cards to scroll to than the
81	 * cap allows; "more history exists" is surfaced via the See-Full-History link (the container's
82	 * own job), not via scrolling this rail further. The scroll/scroll-snap CSS stays
83	 * meaningful only for a real device narrower than the design reference itself (e.g. a phone
84	 * under ~402px), where the capped card count can still slightly overflow the actual viewport.
85	 *
86	 * `cards` is typed as `ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps` (`ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
87	 * ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation`, declared above) — not the full `ZimmProductCardProps`
88	 * union this step's own given component contract originally specified verbatim (narrowed
89	 * 2026-09-15, CodeRabbit finding, confirmed: this component only ever renders the
90	 * `recentlyViewed` variation, so the wider union let a caller pass e.g. a `plp`-shaped card with
91	 * no compile error, even though nothing here would ever render its `plp`-only fields). This
92	 * component therefore still spreads each entry straight into `ZimmProductCard`
93	 * (`<ZimmProductCard {...card} />`) rather than forcing `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` onto every
94	 * card itself — every entry already carries that variation by construction (A3's mapper produces
95	 * `recentlyViewed`-shaped cards) and now by the type itself, since `ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps`
96	 * has no other variation to be. Type-only change: `ZimmProductCard`'s own prop type is still the
97	 * full union, and a `ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps` value is one real member of it, so this compiles
98	 * and renders identically to before.
99	 *
100	 * `data-testid="product-card"` / `data-product-id` on each rendered card come from
101	 * `ZimmProductCard`'s own root (zimmProductCard/index.tsx: "a DOM hook for QA automation/
102	 * analytics") — this component adds no additional per-card test hook of its own.
103	 */
104	export const ZimmRecentlyViewedRail = ({ title, cards, seeAllHref, seeAllLabel }: ZimmRecentlyViewedRailProps) => {
105	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_RECIPE, {});
106	
107	  // Cap is enforced here, client-side, regardless of how many cards were passed in — the data
108	  // source (Einstein's own `recommendations.recs`, wired in build plan step E1) does not itself
109	  // honour a requested limit, and per-breakpoint capping is this component's own presentational
110	  // concern, not the container's. Falls back to the smallest (base/mobile) count on the very first render
111	  // before the client-side media-query match resolves (see RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS's
112	  // own comment, app/constants/index.ts, for why this is a hard per-breakpoint cap, not a "fits
113	  // before scrolling" soft limit). A slice, never a sort — order is otherwise untouched (AC 2).
114	  //
115	  // `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount()`, not a direct `useBreakpointValue` call (corrected
116	  // 2026-09-10 — see that hook's own docblock for the live-confirmed bug this closes): this
117	  // component's own Desktop card-width styling (zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's
118	  // `DESKTOP_UP_QUERY`) switches at 1024px, not this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px) that
119	  // `useBreakpointValue` would have resolved against — the two disagreeing meant a real, narrow
120	  // window (1024–1280px) where cards were already styled for 5 slots but only 3 were allowed to
121	  // render.
122	  const maxVisibleCards = useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount();
123	  const visibleCards = cards.slice(0, maxVisibleCards);
124	
125	  // Second guard behind A4's own visibility gate, which lives in the container, not here — an
126	  // empty rail renders nothing at all, not an empty shell.
127	  if (visibleCards.length === 0) {
128	    return null;
129	  }
130	
131	  return (
132	    <chakra.div __css={styles.container} data-testid="recently-viewed-rail">
133	      <chakra.div __css={styles.header}>
134	        {/* flex/minWidth match Figma's own title node (flex: 1 0 0, min-w-px) — grows to fill
135	            whatever `header`'s own gap + the link's width don't claim, and can shrink below its
136	            own text's intrinsic width rather than force an overflow. See zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's
137	            own "TITLE/LINK SPACING" docblock section. */}
138	        <chakra.span textStyle="heading3" flex="1 0 0" minWidth={0}>
139	          {title}
140	        </chakra.span>
141	        {seeAllHref && seeAllLabel && (
142	          <SeeAllLink to={seeAllHref} textStyle="linkLg" __css={styles.seeAllLink}>
143	            {seeAllLabel}
144	          </SeeAllLink>
145	        )}
146	      </chakra.div>
147	      <chakra.div __css={styles.group} data-testid="recently-viewed-rail-group">
148	        {visibleCards.map((card) => (
149	          <chakra.div key={card.id} __css={styles.card}>
150	            <ZimmProductCard {...card} />
151	          </chakra.div>
152	        ))}
153	      </chakra.div>
154	    </chakra.div>
155	  );
156	};
