## Scale line

This is a whole-feature, step-blind pattern sweep, not a per-step retest — each of the 6 commits was already scored PASS individually. I ran all 7 checks the brief specified (4 internal + 3 external), split across my own direct verification and 3 dispatched sub-agents (Einstein-wiring pattern parity, dead-code repo-wide sweep, rules-conformance/CSS-untouched). I deliberately dropped the standard per-step angles that don't apply to a "did the same fix land everywhere it needed to" sweep on a data-source-swap build with zero new components/recipes/stories: Structure, Storybook interactivity, Accessibility, rendered-layout/visual-checkpoint, stacking-context, and AC-by-AC ticket re-litigation — all vacuous here (nothing new was authored, no rendered output changed, already confirmed independently below) or already the per-step tester's job. I added one thing beyond the 7 named checks: I ran `tsc`/`npm test` myself against current HEAD (`aedbc58`) rather than trust the implementer's own commit-message numbers, since no tester had independently verified the *final* state (the handoff's gate table stops at E4, before the two CR-fix commits). That's a first verification, not a re-run of an unchanged check.

---

## Internal Check 1 — buildUrl site/locale-prefix parity: CLEAN

Verified directly (`git show aedbc58`). Both `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts:213-216` and `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:377-380` take an identically-shaped injected `buildUrl: (path: string) => string` third parameter; both containers (`recommended-products/index.tsx:265`, `recentlyViewed/index.tsx:256`) call `useMultiSite()` and destructure `buildUrl` the same way; both match the pre-established `formatPrice`-injection precedent and cite the identical upstream pattern in `productListCardMapper.ts:273,290`. CONFIRMED, no finding.

## Internal Check 2 + External Check 1 — Einstein-wiring pattern parity: mostly CLEAN, one real asymmetry

Via sub-agent (full file reads of both consumers + `use-einstein.js` source, plus `git show c14ee9f:...` archaeology):
- `getRecommendations(recommender, _products)` (rail, `_products` always `undefined` in practice — confirmed no real caller ever passes `products=` for this recommender) vs. `getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED)` (page, no 2nd arg): **CONFIRMED no behavioral difference** — `use-einstein.js` has no default parameter and never touches `arguments`, so an omitted arg and an explicit `undefined` are identical. ONE-OFF, non-issue.
- Both consumers read `useEinstein()`/`recommendations.recs` identically; the Rail-vs-ProductScroller split and the (pre-existing) absence of click-tracking on the RV branch both predate this 6-commit build, traced to `c14ee9f` and further back to `ab26ee6`. CONFIRMED, not this build's doing.
- **New finding:** `recentlyViewed/index.tsx` has zero impression/click-tracking wiring anywhere in its entire history (`git log --follow`, 9 commits) — no `useDataCloud`, no `isOnScreen`, no `sendViewReco`. Meanwhile the rail's own impression effect, dormant under the interim mechanism, now genuinely fires for real post-build (confirmed by this build's own docblock, `recommended-products/index.tsx:71-76`). Result: the two consumers of the identical `PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` recommender now report asymmetric telemetry to Einstein — one reports view-impressions, the other never has and still doesn't. CONFIRMED. 🟡 should-fix / 🔵 note (pre-existing, not introduced by this build — see "What Marcel is missing"). UNIFORM in shape (incomplete Einstein feedback-loop wiring across a shared recommender's consumers), not something these 6 commits caused.

## Internal Check 3 — empty/loading gate "is this still the ONLY difference": NOT CLEAN — headline finding

I verified this myself directly (not delegated): `git show 5660869` (the CR-fix), current source of both files, and a grep of the rail's own test file.

**What's wrong.** Commit `5660869` found and fixed a real bug in `recentlyViewed/index.tsx`: gating render on Einstein's raw `recs.length` instead of the post-mapping, null-filtered `cards.length` (a shopper with real but 100%-stale history saw a blank page, since `recs.length>0` took the grid branch even though every product failed to map). The fix touched **only** `recentlyViewed/index.tsx`. `recommended-products/index.tsx:346` — the RV branch's identical map→filter→cards shape — still reads `if (!recommendations?.recs?.length) { return null; }`, the pre-mapping check, unchanged.

**Consequence.** The *visible* render outcome is masked: `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` has its own `visibleCards.length === 0 → return null` guard (`zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx:127-129`), so an empty `cards` array still correctly shows nothing — this is exactly why no per-step review caught it. But the impression-tracking effect (`recommended-products/index.tsx:308-325`) fires `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` purely off `recommendations?.recs` being truthy, with **zero reference to `cards`/`visibleCards`**. In the identical "every rec fails to map" scenario the E2 fix targets, the rail will report Einstein view-impressions for products that never rendered — silently polluting the exact feedback signal Einstein uses to judge its own recommendation quality. 🔴 must-fix.

**Compounding.** `recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own docblock (lines 201-208), written as part of the very fix that created this divergence, still asserts the rail's gate follows "the same principle" — no longer true post-fix. 🟡 should-fix (stale/incorrect cross-file claim). And `recommended-products/index.test.tsx` has no test for this scenario at all — grepped for "every"/"all...null"/"all...stale"/"all...offline": zero hits; the only tested empty case is a genuine `recs: []` (line 264); `sendViewReco` is mocked as an unasserted `vi.fn()` in every RV case (lines 184/249/274/304/334/363) — unlike `recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx`, which now has a dedicated, mutation-tested "all-stale-history gate" test for exactly this shape. 🟡 should-fix (test-coverage gap).

This directly answers Marcel's own Internal Check 3: the stated difference (page has a distinct empty-state UI, rail doesn't) is **not** the only difference anymore — a second, unreasoned divergence exists because the fix was applied asymmetrically.

**CONFIRMED** (diff read + current-source read + grep, not inference). **UNIFORM** — the underlying defect shape (gate on a pre-filter count where a post-filter one exists and is correct) is exactly the kind of thing that could recur anywhere else in this codebase's map→filter→render pattern, and here it concretely recurred within this same feature's two consumers.

## Internal Check 4 — dead-code repo-wide sweep: mostly CLEAN, 2 comment-only survivors + a process gap

Independently re-derived (sub-agent ran fresh `rg --hidden` across the whole repo, not trusting the build's claim):
- Zero hits for all 5 named module/constant symbols in tracked/live code — the only 25 grep hits were in `.git/rr-cache` (inert local merge-conflict-resolution cache, never shipped/tracked — correctly identified as harmless, confirmed via `git ls-files -- .git` returning nothing).
- File-existence, `constants/index.ts` direct read, `.claude/registry/*.md`, and `tsc --noEmit` all independently confirmed clean.
- **Real finding:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx:69` and `:125` still describe the deleted hook's `hasRecentlyViewed` output ("A4") as the **current** visibility-gating mechanism, in present tense — the real gate now lives in the container as `!recommendations?.recs?.length` (E1). This file was **not** on the plan's own named stale-comment-sweep list (that list covered `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` references, not the deleted hook's own variable names). 🟡 should-fix, comment-only/zero build impact (confirmed via clean `tsc`).
- **Process-level observation, worth naming as its own finding:** line 125 doesn't even contain the literal string "hasRecentlyViewed" — it only says "A4's own visibility gate." A symbol-name grep, however exhaustive, cannot catch a paraphrased architectural reference to a deleted concept. The E4 cleanup's own pass criteria grepped for deleted *module/constant* names but never included the deleted hook's *return-value* names in that same "prove zero hits" list. UNIFORM: this is a gap in the cleanup **method**, not just this one file — any future grep-gated deletion in this codebase can leave the same kind of prose-only residue behind.

## External Check 2 — rules conformance spot-check: CLEAN except one spelling miss

Independently verified: zero bare Chakra token keys, zero new magic numbers/strings (the only literal recommender string appears inside a comment, not code), zero `.js`/`.jsx` under `overrides/`, token-audit's 3 findings all in files absent from this diff (cross-referenced against the file list, confirmed pre-existing). One real miss: `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx:293` — "Normalized" in new Zimmermann-authored comment prose, house style requires "Normalised" (6 other "colour" instances in the same diff are spelled correctly, so this reads as an isolated slip). 🔵 note / easy 🟡 should-fix. CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.

## External Check 3 — Figma/CSS untouched: CONFIRMED CLEAN

`git diff --stat c14ee9f..aedbc58 -- overrides/app/theme/` and `-- '**/*.css.ts'` are both empty. The two changed `.stories.tsx` files are purely type-import/comment updates (verified by reading both diffs in full) — zero prop/JSX/visual changes. Matches the plan's own claim that this was a pure data-source swap.

## Compiles and passes

`npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0 (ran myself, fresh, against `aedbc58`). `npm run test` → **85 files, 1308 tests, all passing** (ran myself; matches `aedbc58`'s own commit-message claim, now independently corroborated rather than trusted). `recipeGuards.test.ts` ran and passed (6 tests) — vacuous-but-green, since no recipe file was touched by this build.

## Imports — clean (brief, self-verified)

`recommended-products/index.tsx:159` imports `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` via a relative path, not the base SFCC path, matching `overrideStyling.md`'s rule for an already-overridden component, with its own comment explaining why. No `../../../..` chains beyond 2-3 levels in any touched file. No circular imports observed.

---

## What I tried to falsify

Went looking for a place where "the fix landed everywhere it needed to" would be false, and found one (Internal Check 3, above) via direct diff+source+test-grep evidence, not inference. Also tried: a real behavioral difference in the `getRecommendations` argument shape (none — verified against real vendor source); hidden click/view-tracking wiring in the Rail/Card prop surface (none exists); a bare Chakra token, raw literal, magic number, or `.js`/`.jsx` file anywhere in the diff (none); the build's own "zero dead references" claim via a fresh independent grep (held for literal symbol names, did **not** fully hold for paraphrased architectural-label prose — 2 stale comments found).

## What I could not verify

Whether the rail's masked-rendering-but-real-analytics-pollution scenario is reachable in every browser's `IntersectionObserver` behavior for a zero-area target — no live render exists to test against (Einstein is undeployed everywhere reachable, the plan's own stated ceiling). Whether the Full History page's total absence of impression tracking is a deliberate, already-accepted scope decision or a genuine miss — requires the SFCC-84 PRD/AC history, outside a code-only sweep. Whether the "paraphrased stale comment" pattern recurs elsewhere in the repo beyond the one file found — that's a materially larger, different sweep than this one's budget allows, and I did not run it.

---

## What Marcel is missing

The rail's impression-tracking just went live for Recently-Viewed for the first time (this build's own stated, intended side effect), but the Full History page has never had any impression or click tracking at all, in its entire history — so the moment Einstein actually deploys, Einstein/Data Cloud will start receiving real "viewed" signal from PDP/PLP/Cart for this recommender but literally zero signal from the Full History page, even though both surface the same recommender. That asymmetry predates this build and isn't something these 6 commits should fix, but nobody would notice it today (Einstein undeployed everywhere), and it's exactly the kind of gap that looks like "missing data" on a dashboard six months from now with no obvious cause unless someone's told in advance.
